Axiom:
Phase cannot emit Handoff without one successful `sdd-verify --task --phase `. The CLI, not the phase agent, structurally selects and runs the ladder plus every applicable ticket §5 command verbatim, then atomically writes their exact command/role/exit evidence and Target File state as the phase receipt. Any failure writes no reusable receipt and keeps the phase `[~] IN_PROGRESS` until resolved or escalated.
**MANDATORY (PROTOCOL) — Canonical Gate Rule:** Ticket §5 commands are CANONICAL and CANNOT be substituted. Diagnostics may run while fixing, but only the canonical phase command can create completion evidence; a hand-written `ver` line is not evidence.
The canon covers the script's BODY, not just its name in §5. Editing what a §5 script actually runs (e.g. rewriting `"typecheck"` in `package.json` so it does less, or points elsewhere) while logging the unchanged §5 command name is the same violation — the command stayed canonical on paper while its behavior was substituted underneath it. The one exception: `package.json` (or the script body) is itself among this phase's Target Files AND the change to that script IS the phase's stated Objective (a `bootstrap` / `config` phase whose job is exactly to define or rewire the script) — then the edit is legitimate work, not a gate dodge, and MUST be recorded as its own decision line in the Execution Log (` decision rewritten ← `) before the gate runs.
`sdd-verify --task --phase ` is NOT supplemental — it owns STEP_5, including §5 extras (see `AX_PERMITTED_BASH_COMMANDS`). §5 therefore holds only EXTRA commands beyond the standard ladder and never repeats `sdd-verify`.
Phase kind `doc` typically has no verification — empty section is acceptable.
